query: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility in the cast state and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, but inadequate oxygen resistance prevents most practical high-temperature applications. Earlier oxidation-protection research prevented pesting in a related, non-equiatomic Hf–Nb–Ta–Ti–Zr alloy during a 5 h exposure to air at 800 °C, but that result does not establish protection for equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr; related studies on other refractory alloys likewise did not evaluate this composition. With preservation of useful room- and high-temperature mechanical performance as a design constraint, what single intervention could improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr? Formulate one hypothesis identifying the intervention and mechanism, predicting the outcome relative to untreated material, defining the applicable temperature, atmosphere, exposure-time, and loading boundaries, citing supporting evidence from the prior studies, and specifying a controlled experiment and result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: A minor addition of aluminum (≈2 at.%) to equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr will improve its oxygen resistance at high temperatures by promoting the in situ formation of a continuous, adherent Al2O3 scale that slows oxygen ingress, thereby mitigating pesting without degrading the alloy’s room‐temperature ductility or high‐temperature strength.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr exhibiting 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
generation.intervention: Introduce approximately 2 atomic percent of aluminum during melting/casting to create a modified alloy composition.
generation.conditions: Exposure in laboratory air at approximately 800 °C for at least 5 hours under conditions representative of service loading, while also evaluating room-temperature and high-temperature mechanical properties.
generation.structural_mediator: The formation of a thin, coherent, and protective Al2O3 oxide layer on the alloy surface.
generation.mechanism: Aluminum, being a strong oxide former, oxidizes preferentially at elevated temperatures to form a dense Al2O3 scale. This scale acts as an effective diffusion barrier that impedes further oxygen ingress into the substrate, thus reducing pesting and oxidation damage while the low-level addition is expected to preserve the bcc matrix and desirable mechanical properties.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to the untreated equiatomic alloy, the Al-modified alloy is predicted to show a significantly lower mass gain (indicating slower oxidation kinetics) and a more uniform, adherent oxide scale after 5 hours of exposure at 800 °C. Its room-temperature ductility and high-temperature yield strength should remain within the useful range.
generation.baseline: Untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr, which demonstrates inadequate oxygen resistance (rapid oxidation and pesting) under the same exposure conditions.
generation.boundary: This intervention is expected to be effective for exposures around 800 °C in air for durations of 5 hours (and possibly longer) while maintaining mechanical performance; effects outside these temperature–time bounds have not been established.
generation.uncertainty: Exactly how much Al is optimal and whether minor alloying may subtly affect phase stability or other mechanical properties requires further detailed investigation.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of cast samples: one set of the standard equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr and one set with an additional ~2 at.% Al. Expose both sets to air at 800 °C for 5 hours. After exposure, perform quantitative mass gain measurements, investigate the oxide scale using SEM (and possibly XRD) to assess its thickness and adhesion, and conduct tensile tests at room temperature as well as yield strength measurements after high-temperature exposure.
measurements: Mass gain per unit area (oxidation kinetics)
Oxide scale morphology, continuity, and thickness (via SEM/XRD)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Al-modified alloy does not display a statistically significant reduction in oxidation-induced mass gain and does not exhibit a uniform, adherent Al2O3 scale relative to the untreated alloy, or if its mechanical performance (ductility or strength) falls outside the acceptable range, then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Paper card. Question: What is the oxidation behavior of the refractory AlNbTiVZr 0.25 high-entropy alloy at temperatures between 600 and 900 °C?. System: AlNbTiVZr 0.25 (nominal composition: Al 25.0, Nb 22.4, Ti 24.0, V 21.9, Zr 6.7 at.%). Processing: Arc melting in low-pressure high-purity argon; homogenization at 1200 °C for 24 h; specimens cut via electric discharge machine and polished with colloidal silica suspension. Test conditions: Static lab air at 600, 700, and 800 °C for 100 h, and 900 °C for 50 h; mass measurements at intervals of 0.5, 1, 5, 10, 20, 50, and 100 h.
